items.title: Award in Supporting Individuals with Disabilities at the Workplace
items.description:
Training targeted towards individuals who are motivated to enable inclusion of persons with disability in the workplace,  who have the drive to coach and support these persons who have disabilities such as but not limited to,  intellectual,  social/communication and physical disabilities.
Attain a sound general knowledge through recognizing and understanding socio- economic aspect of disability and inclusion in general; Develop an understanding of the nature of and potential causes of the various challenges that individuals with disability face; Be aware of the potential impact that environmental stressors may have on the individual with disability; Attain basic knowledge of the local legislation and the labour market regarding individuals with disabilities in employment; Describe the diagnostic aspect and potential causes that lead to the individual being diagnosed with an intellectual disability; Identify the potential impact that various stressors may have on the individual with  an intellectual disability; Find the basic strategies utilized when working with individuals with intellectual disability; List the various challenges involved when facilitating individuals with disability; Define specialized approaches and strategies and the importance of their implementation to facilitate inclusion. Significant knowledge through the understanding of the manifestations of different intellectual disabilities; Identify difficulties and liaise with other professionals for further specific recommendations and is able to carry these out. Evaluate potential difficulties and refers for assistance to address these issues; Propose basic support strategies that may be applied in different setting; Analyze and identify the areas which may be impaired and are a priority to be addressed to enable the facilitation of inclusion at the workplace; Describe and discuss general observations made regarding the impairments and challenges that may be present in persons with disability and who need to be included with other relevant stakeholders; Interact effectively with persons with disability to enhance communication; Review and report any information related to the individual’s well-being and development; Illustrate support strategies during intervention and the facilitation of inclusion at the workplace; State the main support strategies that should be applied when facilitating inclusion at the workplace.

items.title: Award in Customs Procedures
items.description:
This course provides learners with the knowledge and skills needed to identify the major players in international trade; recognise the main Acts,  Regulations,  and Policies related to international trade; and understand the roles of the importer,  exporter,  customs broker,  and carrier. The aim of this course is to introduce the learners to trade,  business opportunities and export/import processes. Throughout the unit,  candidates will obtain knowledge of the operational and strategic roles of customs in daily decision making and of the cooperation with Customs' usual internal and external partners in daily activities. Furhermore,  candidates will gain a high level understanding of customs processes and how they are interlinked,  understand the business drivers and the macro and micro economics related to a national,  EU and global context. The project requires understanding the scope of customs legislation and its legal definitions and Cusotms regulations,  as well as other regulations that affect Customs operations,  such as health,  environmental and security related regulations.The course format is classroom based. Finally,  learners will have the ability to effectively apply this knowledge during their daily work.
Evaluate the fundamental knowledge of the procedures for each customs domain as defined by the UCC. Communicate effectively using basic international business vocabulary with specific emphasis on terms associated with trade and import / export operations. Assess the documentation requirements of the exporter / importer to comply with Customs Regulations within the supply chain. Identify the most beneficial and applicable customs procedure under different circumstances. Identify the basic laws and procedures in place including national and EU regulations.

items.title: Award in Data Analytics,  GIS and Earth Observation
items.description:
This is a bespoke course designed for a local authority. The aim of this course is to empower the learner with tools and techniques to visualise data so to undertake analytical analysis,  identify patterns and infer knowledge in other areas. The tools referred to here,  must have a data analystics,  Geographical Information Systems (GIS) and/or Eearth Observation (EO) scope and purpose limited to User Interface (UI). The course will follow a use-case approach focusing on matters of an environmental and climate change benefit/impact.
Identify Geographic Information Systems and Earth Observation Tools concepts and techniques. Use information from data sources to undertake geographical and earth observational studies. Utilise data analytical tools to visualise data and extract patterns of relevance. Report findings in visual and interactive manners to support undertaken studies.

items.title: Advanced Diploma in Manufacturing Technology (Food-bespoke)
items.description:
This is a bespoke course designed for private industry. This course will provide the candidate with the necessary knowledge and skills in the technological area of manufacturing engineering. This course is intended for candidates who wish to progress in their career as technicians in Manufacturing Technology.  This provides candidates with a solid technical competence and understanding of the regulations and health and safety requirements governing the electrical installation industry. This course also contains modules related to Engineering and Electronic Control Systems that give candidates a solid grounding in the engineering involved in the building services industry. Candidates will also receive exposure to Mechanical and Electrical Workshop Practice for a more holistic training programme. Apart from preparing students to become fully fledged technicians,  the course design also prepares students for further studies at degree level should they so desire.

Design,  perform and test industrial electrical installations and machinery according to regulations and requirements Work safely,  communicate effectively in a team,  and take responsibility of work in a manufacturing context. Identify health and environmental risk related to manufacturing technologies and engineering. Troubleshoot,  repair,  and modify existing industrial electrical installations,  motors,  and switchgear.

The course will cover 60 ECTS. It will have three modules,  namely: (i) Economics and Environmental Studies (ii) History and (ii) Culture. Each module will consist of 5 study units (4 ECTS each). items.title: Award in Principles of Child Development and Appropriate Teaching Practices (Childhood Development)
items.description:
In this module, students will study various concepts and topics related to child development and learning principles. Each topic will be situated within the context of the classroom environment, the child’s developmental stage and/or recommendations for best classroom practices.

 Students will be responsible for observing, attending lectures, and completing readings and assignments that may include modelling and role play to demonstrate their understanding of the concepts discussed. Some of the topics addressed in this module include: the role of work and playful learning in child’s development; strategies on how to inspire children to choose and sustain work; creating awareness of the ways instructors/teachers may be unintentionally forcing children to choose work or play; critical assessment of interventions and invitation strategies; strategies for troubleshooting issues that may arise in a learning environment.
At the end of the module/unit the learner will be able to: 
a) Evaluate and implement developmentally appropriate methods and curricula for guiding children.

b) Explain and apply strategies and techniques of role play and modelling related to best classroom practices for each developmental stage.

c) Show understanding of the Principles of Developmental Crises and strategies for teaching children at these stages. At the end of the module/unit the learner will have acquired the following skills: 

a) Ability to apply theoretical and practical knowledge in the creation of solutions for problems related to child development.

b) Communicate ideas in a well-structured, professional manner, following appropriate conventions. 

c) Can select appropriate evidence when formulated responses to well-defined concrete and abstract problems of child development. At the end of the module/unit the learner will have acquired the responsibility and autonomy to:
a) Plan and implement instruction by applying knowledge of environmental and biological factors that can restrain the development of a young child’s learning.

b) Reflect on and analyse teaching and nurturing practices and how they interrelate with principles of child development.

c) Implement key Montessori materials and practices through presentations and lessons.

d) Demonstrate effective communication in a classroom setting.

items.title: Award in Primary Health
items.description:
This module will help introduce participants to community healthcare in the primary health setting. It will provide necessary knowledge for healthier living. The participants will enhance their knowledge on the prevention and rehabilitation care within the community setting. It will emphasize on the importance of promoting fairness when offering health services to the present culturally diverse population.
 This module will introduce the participants to Primary Health Care within a community health setting.

The module discusses the model of Primary Health Care which is currently being used at national level which addresses 3 main components.  The first component addresses how primary health care meets people’s health throughout their life by offering public services within the community setting.  This it does by promoting equity and fairness to the national multicultural population.
The second component of Primary Health Care looks at a wider view and addresses broader elements of health which include environmental health related aspects. The Primary Health Care system is also responsible for promoting education on health.  This third component is primarily aimed at empowering individuals, families, and the community to improve on their health.

This Module provides also information regarding access and functions of the diverse services offered at the different public health centers and clinics within the community.

This module focuses on the Maltese Primary Health Care model.
•	Be able to have an understanding of the importance of having appropriate nursing skills which include patient assessment and evaluation techniques;
•	Be able to have an understanding of the importance of maintaining the principles of environmental health in community education
•	Be able to have an understanding of the importance of appropriated techniques to solve problems in community settings. •	Develop a comprehensive understanding of primary care programme and services provided in Malta and Gozo;
•	Identify the challenges of environmental health;
•	Understand terms and stages of prevention and how they can be applied; •	Providing continuity of care for individuals in the community
•	The importance of illness prevention
•	The patient assessment and evaluation 
•	Health promotion –raising awareness 
•	The challenges when providing care in different community settings
•	Surrounding environment and its effect on ones’ health
•	Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct for Nurses and Midwives, Council for Nurses and Midwives, Malta, January 2020

items.title: Award in Strategic Management
items.description:
This unit will provide the students with a comprehensive consolidated framework for understanding the responsibility and purposes of Strategic Management inside modern-day business organisations. Students will understand how different entities formulate,  implement,  and evaluate strategies and how they consider the strategic alternatives available to them. The students will also be provided with a framework and context within which knowledge acquired across the course may be combined with new strategic-management techniques and how this may be integrated to outline the future prospective direction of different businesses. items.title: Award in Physiological Psychology
items.description:
This is offered as an exit point to the programme entitled BSc(Hons)Investigative Criminology and Criminal Psychology.  Physiological psychology is a branch of behavioural neuroscience (but also of psychology) that studies behaviour related to physiological functions. Physiological psychology,  which represents a bridge between neuroscience and psychology,  aims to explain how and to what extent the physiology of the human brain influences mental processes and behaviour. The preparatory teaching for the university studies of psychology is usually “psychophysiology”,  which studies the opposite mechanism,  that is how an organism reacts to psychological stimuli. However,  considering the great neuroscientific discoveries that have been made since the 1990s,  showing that deviant or criminal behaviour is only partially due to psychosocial or environmental conditions,  it was decided to start this course from brain physiology. While psychophysiology studies how the psyche affects the health of the organism,  physiological psychology studies how the organism acts on behaviour. While the psychology student has to study psychophysiology to know how psychological states affect health,  the criminologist is interested in understanding how physical conditions can influence a person's behaviour. The award teaches the student an overview of the physiological functions that influence human behaviour. In this way,  the forensic criminologist will be able to better understand the reports of forensic neurologists or forensic psychiatrists who collaborate on a forensic case. In order to educate competent criminologist who can work as a consultant with police officers,  they will have to be able to make valuable contribution in managing emergency situations in which people are under stress/duress. The award of Physiological Psychology represents the basic knowledge for students aiming to further study subjects such as Neurocriminology and criminological sciences applied to emergency situations.
Interpret the sense and meaning of physiological psychology;  Create the conditions for a better observation of physiological phenomena of behaviour; Autonomously reach conclusions regarding the results of research conducted on the topics covered in this module; Sustain conversations about the topics of this module using a correct scientific terminology; Correctly interpret scientific texts regarding neurosciences; Conduct in-depth research on neuroscientific topics. Self-study of the teaching material developed by the lecturer and of the recommended textbook; Personal research activity assigned by the lecturer and discussed with the lecturer;  Discussion and analysis of real cases;  The interaction with the lecturer will be through digital communication channels (e-mail,  virtual meetings,  etc.). Use the gained knowledge to understand how behavioural problems are detected,  both with traditional and modern techniques of neuroimaging; Communicate information,  ideas,  problems and solutions in the context of a basic neuroscientific research; Interact with medical-forensic experts,  such as coroners,  psychiatrists and forensic neuropsychologists;  Know physiological mechanisms on which decisional processes are based; Combine the knowledge of psychology applied to the management of critical contexts with the knowledge offered by modern neurosciences.

items.description:
The Diploma course is a one-year day course. The students are considered as regular University students. During the first semester,  all students follow all study units and an optional study unit. During the second semester,  students may follow one stream of specialization,  animal science,  crop science or herb science. Those students who choose the animal science stream,  have to follow a crop production study unit in the first semester,  while students who choose the crop or herb science streams,  have to follow an animal production study unit in the first semester. In the second semester,  alongside the specialisation streams,  students follow a study unit on food systems and have to prepare a report on a topic,  chosen and agreed upon earlier during the year.
The students gain knowledge and experience on rural sciences and food systems. They will be able to tackle agricultural problems and perceive agriculture as part of a rural,  environmental and urban ecosystem.

items.title: Higher Education Award in Developing Environmental Responsibility
items.description:
While the course is focused on Developing Environmental Responsibility, this is explored within the context of the environmental and social problems that societies around the world are facing. In other words, the focus is on the processes and actions through which people, as individuals and communities, avoid the depletion of natural resources, in order to keep an ecological balance that does not allow the quality of life of societies to decrease, but rather enhances the well-being of all. In other words, Environmental Responsibility is not explored on its own, but rather as it intersects with social, economic, and cultural realities: hence the link between environmental responsibility and sustainability is made explicit.  This reflects historical developments like the Earth Summit of 1992, where the Environment was no longer considered on its own but in conjunction with Development. It is also in synch with the Sustainable Development Goals, where it is widely recognised that any efforts to tackle climate change and preserve the environment needs to go hand in hand with ending poverty, improving health and education, and reducing inequality. 
Thus, the concept of developing environmental responsibility is presented as an ideal entry point to examine ones own and community’s lifestyle, including our roles as consumers, and within the current understanding of sustainable development and regeneration. 
This positioning is also reflected in the main text being proposed, namely Laudato si', which calls for an ecological conversion, where the pleading for an integral ecology calls upon us all to hear both the cry of the poor and the cry of the Earth. The understanding today is that Laudato sì has both an ecological and a social message, where everything is connected, and where the intersecting concerns of environmental responsibility and authentic human development are addressed.
The unit will help students understand the complexity of environmental and sustainability issues, see new opportunities to be part of the solutions and develop a sense of responsibility towards the protection of their environment. The unit creates opportunities for learners to know how they can further translate this responsibility into action through practical lifestyle choices. 

The unit helps students position themselves in a vast universe of information and orient them towards a shared problem-solving endeavour.
	Conduct a self-evaluation to gauge their ecological footprint and plan how to reduce it accordingly
	Apply critical thinking skills to develop environmental responsibility and bring about sustainable choices in their personal day-to-day life
	Apply critical thinking skills to improve the environment and bring about sustainable change at a household, institution, and community level. 	Reflect critically on their roles and identities as active citizens, consumers and change agents in a complex and interconnected world
	Reduce their ecological footprint
	Contribute to “whole organisation change” at their workplace, with respect to greening of the organisation. 	The current basic national and global environmental, social and development challenges, namely as pertaining to biodiversity & nature; climate change; energy; food; waste; water; use of resources and poverty; inequality, and access to resources. 
	A basic understanding of Integral Ecology.

items.title: Award in Introduction to Business and Management
items.description:
Introduction to Business & Management is a foundation module that aims to provide learners with a broad view on key management topics, concepts and issues within the local as well as the global business environment. The aim of this module is to provide a solid base that will support and initiate learners through the concepts of business and management.
a) Underlying management principles (such as Henry Fayol’s 14 principles) of a range of management functions.
b) The core elements of macroeconomics (GDP, economic output, inflation and employment) and their relevance to business organisations 

c) A broad understanding of major theoretical frameworks and approaches to management within business contexts such as Douglas McGregor’s X&Y theory, and Frederick Taylor’s scientific theory.
d) Different concepts and role of management functions (such as planning, organising, staffing, directing) and how these contribute to business success.
e) A variety of organisational understandings and corresponding responsibilities (legal, corporate, people, environmental, community, and ethical) within the local and broader global context  
f) The core elements of effective management practices such as delegation, leadership, problem solving.
g) The different levels of management found in organisations
h) The different roles managers take on in different organisational settings The learner will be able to:

a) Thoughtfully and fairly apply theoretical frameworks identified above to explain differences between organisations operating in a range of sectors, industries, and contexts.
b) Critically assess the organisational responsibilities of businesses such as those related to human talent and engagement, sustainability and the environment, ethics, and finance.
c) Progressively evaluate the nature, importance, and seriousness of the challenges related to different management functions
d) Analytically examine the desired skill sets of a range of manager roles
e) Compare and contrast the different roles managers need to adopt in a range of settings and situations

items.title: Undergraduate Certificate (UGCert) in Childhood Development: Early Childhood ESL Education
items.description:
The programme teaches students comprehensive and specialised subjects in early childhood development and education; it develops skills complementary to the UNESCO Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) which support early childhood development and universal pre-primary education. Specifically, students develop skill in in critical thinking and strategic planning for changing and fast-paced learning environments, including curriculum development, assessment methods, and environmental and behavioural analysis which furthers the pursuit for the global availability of quality education for young learners. Additionally, the programme develops competences in leadership, including autonomous decision-making, and communication with stakeholders, and other members of an educational community to advocate for, create, and sustain meaningful partnerships, policies, and practices that ultimately lead to a version of education based on the principles of human rights, dignity, inclusion, and protection.
a) Students will have knowledge of Early Childhood Education theory and practice that builds upon advanced general education in this field, and by the end of the programme their knowledge will include some aspects informed by findings from empirical research in early childhood education at the forefront of their field of study. b) Students will have theoretical knowledge of Early childhood education commensurate and consistent with scholarship in the field and evidence an awareness of new knowledge in relation to curriculum and pedagogy emerging from research in the field. c) Students will be able to contextualise factual knowledge in view of relevant social and ethical issues pertaining to early childhood education. d)Students will be able to display creative thinking on the basis of the knowledge they gain in the course in response to concrete and abstract problems encountered by educators in the field. a) Students will be able to demonstrate some application of theoretical and practical knowledge in responding to issues encountered in a variety of early childhood learning environments. b) Students will be able to formulate their ideas in clearly-structured conventional formats and use appropriate evidence to support their claims. c) Students will be able to monitor, evaluate, and adjust their own learning needs in order to succeed as independent learners. d) Students both collect data on aspects of early childhood education practice, they interpret the data to interpret and address either problems in their practice or conceptual dilemmas in the field. e) Students will be able to manage well-scoped projects in early childhood education practice that require students to make independent decisions and navigate the complex system of early childhood education. f) Students develop professionalism, discipline, and creativity in managing projects and engaging with other people. g) Students develop the learning skills needed to continue to undertake further, self-directed studies with a high degree of autonomy.
